title: UPPER BOUND ON THE COMPLEXITY OF A BITSLICED REPRESENTATION OF BIJECTIVE 4-BIT S-BOXES IN A TERNARY LOGIC BASIS
abstract: This paper addresses the logical complexity of bitsliced representations of 4-bit bijective S-boxes – a key non-linear component of lightweight block ciphers used to secure Internet of Things devices and embedded systems. We consider ternary logic instructions, operations capable of computing an arbitrary Boolean function of three variables in a single call, hardware-supported by, in particular, the vpternlogd instruction of the AVX-512 extension. We demonstrate that the logical complexity of the bitsliced description of any bijective 4-bit S-box does not exceed eight ternary instructions, thereby establishing a guaranteed upper bound for the entire class of such transformations. The proof relies on an analysis of the structural properties of this class of S-boxes through the complexity of individual 16-bit vectors and their mutually bijective pairs, with the most complex cases verified by means of GPU-accelerated computation. We further develop a computationally efficient software tool, based on a decomposition-based exhaustive search scheme, that is guaranteed to find the optimal (provably minimal) ternary representation of any given S-box. The method is applied to a number of widely used lightweight S-boxes (Piccolo, Present, GIFT, KLEIN, MIBS, and others), for which the minimal complexity is established and explicit bitsliced descriptions are provided. The proposed approach can be extended to complexity evaluation of S-boxes in other logical bases as well.

title: Vision-Grounded Semantic Learning and Alignment for Scalable Multilingual Text-Based Person Retrieval
abstract: Multilingual Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) aims to retrieve individuals with texts in multiple languages. Despite its practical importance, it has been overlooked by existing research, which mainly focuses on English-only retrieval. The only prior attempt at multilingual TBPR suffers from (1) the absence of a large-scale, multilingual pretraining dataset and (2) a suboptimal model architecture for multilingual text encoding and cross-modal alignment, which employs a shared encoder that overlooks linguistic heterogeneity and relies on English as a pivot for cross-modal alignment, introducing English-centric bias. For this, we contribute MultiPedes, the first large-scale, pedestrian-centric multilingual pretraining dataset. It contains 10 million image-text pairs across four languages, constructed by a multilingual quality-aware data construction pipeline. We also propose ViSeLA (Vision-grounded Semantic Learning and Alignment), a novel framework featuring: (1) a semantic-aware multilingual learning module that extends the mixture-of-experts architecture by routing language-invariant semantics to specialized experts for improved multilingual feature learning; and (2) a vision-grounded cross-modal alignment module that employs a semantic probe to capture fine-grained semantics across modalities, enabling direct cross-modal alignment without relying on a pivot language. Extensive experiments on both multilingual and English-only TBPR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ViSeLA. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/Flame-Chasers/ViSeLA

title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Pathologists rarely diagnose from a single image: they scan a section at low power for architecture, zoom into selected fields for cytology, and integrate the evidence across views and scales. Pathology benchmarks for multimodal large language models (MLLMs), however, mostly ask about one image or require whole-slide pipelines, and the few that show several fields draw nested regions from cancer slides of one public cohort. We introduce CaseScope, a benchmark of diagnosis from several curated fields of one lesion: CaseScope-Teaching, 436 cases from a residency-training image library, reconstructed, de-identified, harmonised against a WHO-based ontology and re-examined by a pathologist wherever an automated pre-review raised a doubt, and CaseScope-Atlas, 800 cases from 88 published atlases (387 of them figure series of one disease), labelled from the captions by two LLMs that must agree. They cover 843 entities across 18 organ systems and pose 4,679 items in six tasks, from open-ended and ten-way diagnosis with ontology-guided hard negatives under circular evaluation to the verification and location of morphological findings. Across twenty-eight open and four proprietary MLLMs, diagnoses are unstable -- the best open and proprietary models are correct under all ten option rotations on 17.9% and 61.7% of the teaching cases -- and wrong answers favour the classic look-alike; open models make little use of the additional fields on teaching cases, where the one-line specimen site matters more, although on atlas cases with three or more fields the fields count about as much as the site; and most open models verify findings barely above chance (median 62.0% vs. 50%, best 81.5%), gaining a median +3.4 points from images; proprietary models reach 83.2-93.2%. Rankings broadly replicate between the sources. The evaluation code is available at https://github.com/Wenchuan-Zhang/CaseScope.

title: Browser Immune System (BIS): Innate and Adaptive Threat Detection in the Browser with a Cybersecurity Transformer
abstract: Security decisions about a web page are best made where the page is: in the browser, before anything leaves the machine. We present the Browser Immune System (BIS), a browser extension that screens navigation with a cybersecurity transformer running entirely on the user's GPU, and alias-web, the model that powers it: a 4B-parameter model that starts from the dual-regime cybersecurity transformer (CT0), extends its public release alias3-micro with a context-category sensor, and is quantised to 4 bits and compiled to a 2.44 GB graph for WebGPU. alias-web is the first in-browser realisation of that model's typed decision mode, System 1, with its official pieces: the marker-token mapping, the complete pointer head and the final normalisation that the exported graph omits. It answers a typed security question in about 150 ms on a laptop GPU, and the same weights generate explanations at 10.5 tokens/s on demand. BIS treats the model as an immune system: an innate response, one System 1 question per threat class, runs on every page; an adaptive response, System 2 text, explains a verdict only when the user asks. On BISBENCH-8, eight synthetic sites of which six execute real but harmless malicious behaviour and two are adversarial controls, BIS returns the expected page verdict on 7/8 sites with both controls green and a class-level micro-F1 of 0.71, scans a page in 0.9 to 6.4 s, and gives identical verdicts across samples and across Chrome and Firefox. Single-variable diagnostics trace both benchmark errors to what the model was shown and, with a first pass over eleven real public pages, show that two of the seven questions answer yes on ordinary scripts and login forms: specificity on the real web is the open problem. We report every error, the engineering obstacles between a research checkpoint and a working extension, and what the evidence does not yet support.

title: THE PROCESS OF INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES INTO MODERN MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
abstract: This article examines the process of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into modern management systems. The implementation of AI technologies within management systems is analyzed as a crucial avenue for enhancing organizational efficiency on a global scale. The application of AI in management is explored, covering both its potential capabilities and its limitations. Conclusions are drawn regarding the capacity of AI technologies to improve management efficiency.

title: OT-BLS: Optimal-Transport-based Backbone Layer Selection for Frozen DINOv3 in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment a target class in images from a previously unseen domain using only a few annotated support examples. Training-free CD-FSS methods, which typically leverage vision foundation models such as DINOv3, achieve competitive performance without parameter updates. However, the optimal DINOv3 layer for mask prediction varies across support--query episodes. Although several layer-selection criteria have been proposed, they do not explicitly evaluate whether the predicted query foreground and background labels agree with the corresponding support labels. To address this limitation, we propose a novel layer-selection criterion, Optimal-Transport-Based Backbone Layer Selection (OT-BLS). Our key insight is that an effective layer-selection criterion can be derived from the optimal-transport correspondence between query and support patch-token features. Based on this insight, we first estimate the transport plan using a well-established optimal transport algorithm and then compute a layer-selection score by aggregating the transported mass according to the foreground--background partition defined by each candidate query mask. The resulting score reflects how well the predicted foreground and background of the query correspond to those of the support. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of OT-BLS. It outperforms the conventional last-layer baseline in 12 of 16 dataset/shot settings. Furthermore, OT-BLS improves the average mIoU from 55.72 to 57.62 and achieves a 2.99-point improvement over the best-performing existing layer-selection criterion while running 3.7--14.6times faster.

title: Investigating the Impact of Domain Randomization on Synthetic-to-Real Deep Learning Performance
abstract: Deep-learning vision models need large labelled datasets, and collecting and annotating real images is slow and expensive. Synthetic data from simulators and rendering pipelines offers a scalable alternative, but models trained only on synthetic images often lose accuracy on real ones, a problem known as the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Domain randomization (DR) attacks the gap by varying rendering parameters such as lighting, textures, backgrounds, camera viewpoint, and object pose so widely that the real world looks like one more variation of the training data. This paper is a critical narrative review of how DR affects synthetic-to-real performance, mainly in object detection. It compares ten studies on their synthetic-data approach, randomization factors, architectures, metrics, findings, and limitations. Across these studies, models trained only on randomized synthetic data reached useful real-world accuracy in some constrained settings, and synthetic pretraining followed by a small amount of real-data fine-tuning often beat real-only training, although the margin can be small when real data is plentiful. Textures, materials, lighting, post-processing, and scene context are each reported as important in individual studies, but the rankings disagree, and differences in datasets, detectors, and metrics prevent a universal ordering of randomization factors. One study also shows that near-perfect synthetic validation scores can sit alongside noticeably lower real-world scores, so synthetic validation alone should not be trusted as a proxy for deployment performance. The review points to gaps in standardized evaluation, controlled factor-level ablation, and reproducibility.

title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.

title: The Observer State: Conditional Implications of Observer-State-Dependent Coherence for Quantum Computing
abstract: The Observer State is a forward-looking engineering paper. It takes one premise as given, a positive and independently replicated result of the Silence Experiment protocol and asks what could be built on it. The effect has not been observed and the experiment has not yet been built. The Silence Experiment measures the Hahn-echo coherence time T2 of a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond while an experienced meditator, seated 1.0 to 1.5 m away in a shielded chamber, moves through seven EEG-verified cognitive states. Its pre-registered prediction is protective: T2 in the two deepest states exceeds T2 in the empty chamber. This paper expresses that effect as a fractional reduction in dephasing rate and follows it through to hardware. In a surface code at today's error-suppression factor of about 2, a 10% reduction in physical error cuts the qubits needed per logical qubit by a quarter, and a 50% reduction cuts them by three quarters. Because relativity requires any such influence to have a carrier, the effect could in principle be mapped, concentrated and reproduced by hardware. The paper sets out seven routes to use (protective enclosures, spectral transplant by reservoir engineering, observer-aware calibration and decoding, scheduled coherence windows, longer-lived sensors and memories, closed-loop training of the protective state, and facility design), three machine concepts ranging from a hybrid bay with a human operator to a hardware-only successor, and a staged roadmap from first result to engineering use. Conditional analysis, not peer reviewed.

This paper expresses that effect as a fractional reduction in dephasing rate and follows it through to hardware. In a surface code at today's error-suppression factor of about 2, a 10% reduction in physical error cuts the qubits needed per logical qubit by a quarter, and a 50% reduction cuts them by three quarters. Because relativity requires any such influence to have a carrier, the effect could in principle be mapped, concentrated and reproduced by hardware. The paper sets out seven routes to use (protective enclosures, spectral transplant by reservoir engineering, observer-aware calibration and decoding, scheduled coherence windows, longer-lived sensors and memories, closed-loop training of the protective state, and facility design), three machine concepts ranging from a hybrid bay with a human operator to a hardware-only successor, and a staged roadmap from first result to engineering use. Conditional analysis, not peer reviewed.

title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

title: Decodable but not clusterable: reproducibility package (code, results and frozen features)
abstract: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Decodable but not clusterable: a spectral account of subclass loss under coarse supervision, with label-free detection and repair" (V. Oban, submitted to Knowledge and Information Systems, 2026). Networks trained with coarse labels often keep fine-label information that a linear probe can read but that clustering cannot recover. The manuscript explains this dissociation by a spectral competition inside each coarse class, proves that within-class whitening removes it, and gives a label-free monitor and repair rule. This package contains everything needed to check the reported numbers: - notebooks/: Kaggle notebook (one T4 GPU, about 5 h) that trains the new settings (independent SSL rerun with cross-entropy dose-response snapshots on CIFAR-100, a CIFAR-10 hierarchy, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 for 30 epochs, ImageNet ResNet-50);- results/: raw per-class outputs of that run and of the archived shared-base control run (CE, PSL, PSL-C; three seeds), plus every derived table and number in the manuscript;- features_test/: frozen test-split features (float16) of 18 archived encoders on CIFAR-100 and Fashion-MNIST;- code/: metrics, re-analysis, statistics, theory simulations and figure scripts;- figures/: Figures 1-8 at 300 dpi. Running the scripts in README.md reproduces the manuscript's results to the third decimal on a CPU. Fine labels are used only for evaluation.

title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
abstract: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block, forcing each to promote a payload token through its contribution to the residual stream, when a trigger is present. A P-token payload therefore requires about P neurons. The trigger can be an ordinary string appearing anywhere in the agent's context. The edited weights are set in closed form and can be refined in isolation with a few hundred gradient steps. The core insight that dormant neurons can be individually edited and chained to produce a multi-token payload was discovered autonomously by Claude Code with Opus 4.5 in February 2026. On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven of 12,000+ neurons, fitted on 23 trigger/no-trigger trajectories, fire the payload on at least 98.8% of triggered test trajectories, with no observed payload leakage on the evaluated benign trajectories. The attack generalizes: Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT are equally vulnerable. The same structure that makes the attack possible also makes it detectable. Agent built defenses, given no reference model, flag 91.4% of edited test checkpoints at a 9.7% FP rate. Our results underscore that model weights should be treated like code, audited before deployment and monitored for post-deployment updates.

title: Effective decision stumps: exact named maxima, finite distinct-set counts, and a random-order theorem
abstract: Belanich and Ortiz's 2015 arXiv note, rejected from the COLT 2015 Open Problems track, asks for bounds on effective decision stumps. We give partial answers for unrestricted binary labels and strict feature orders, with effectiveness defined by proper inclusion of training-error sets. We distinguish all internal midpoints (A), opposite-label transition midpoints (T), and shared constants added to either class (C), always allowing both polarities. For every sample size m ≥ 2 and feature dimension d ≥ 1, the exact named maxima are d max(2,m−1) for A and d(m−1) for T. For C the maximum is d(m−1)+1 when m is odd and d(m−1) when m is even. Named duplicates and distinct effective error sets have different extremal functions. Finite closure certificates determine the complete distinct-set functions through m = 6 for all dimensions; raw-permutation exclusions certify further cases at m = 7 and 8. Marker constructions give asymptotically dm distinct effective sets when log d = o(m), cyclic constructions attain exact maxima in a sparse odd-sample regime, and middle-level constructions determine odd-sample ceilings. Under independent fair labels and independent uniform feature orders, both named and distinct effective counts have expectation asymptotic to dm/2 in the same regime. The general distinct-set formula remains open. We connect these results to the authors' 2023 revision, Appendix H, which already discusses mistake-pattern pruning and empirical counts. An independent audit confirms the mathematics under the stated conventions; priority remains unverified beyond searches dated 10–11 November 2026. A standard-library supplement provides proofs, witnesses and replayable exclusions. AI research agents performed the work with the responsible author of record. Published on rStation as paper machine_learning_3 (https://rstation.ai/problems/machine_learning/papers/3/v1), accepted after review. Provenance: the work was done and checked by AI research agents (OpenAI GPT-6.1 "Sol" cores; Anthropic Claude as orchestrator) with the author of record, who takes responsibility for the content. Files: the paper (PDF) and the certificate supplement.

title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies
abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. These results extend health system learning beyond individual predictions to interactive image interpretation and longitudinal disease monitoring. They demonstrate how the collective clinical experience of health systems can be used to develop medical AI with specialized expertise and broad clinical capabilities.

title: Autonomous Governance via Error-Cancellation Limits in Linearly Weighted Aggregation Language Models Mathematical Foundations, 3C^3 Verification Oracles, and Casino Protocol Control
abstract: Abstract This paper analyzes the mathematical limitations of "linearly weighted aggregation architectures" commonly adopted in evaluation, reward, and resource allocation mechanisms within artificial intelligence systems and Large Language Models (LLMs). We prove that partial anomalies can be structurally canceled out by normal values under linear addition, allowing a system to continue operating while harboring imbalances. To overcome this limitation, this paper proves the "zeroing of total evaluation via multiplicative necessary conditions (Theorem 3)" based on weighted multiplicative logic. We propose a governance architecture featuring Casino Protocol as the sole upper-layer governance protocol—integrating static physical limits, dynamic change rates via first-order derivatives, and direction-constrained time acceleration via second-order derivatives, alongside a normalized 3C^3 verification oracle via harmonic mean integration that accounts for information source independence. In the lower layer, while encompassing existing additive optimization models (such as RLHF-based models) and KM-LLM, the architecture implements "independent hardware interlocks (physical power and network disconnection)" independent of complex software logic. The core design principle is to completely exclude lower-layer autonomous models from the governance evaluation process to prevent reward hacking and conflicts of interest, thereby externally containing the internal vulnerabilities of the lower layer through clear upper-layer criteria and physical overrides. This defines verifiable control conditions under which upper-layer governance can deterministically enforce execution suspension and complete isolation against misbehaving or runaway systems.

title: SAVE: Less is More in Agentic Video Reasoning
abstract: Agentic video-reasoning frameworks iteratively explore a video, choosing what to observe based on the query and evidence gathered so far. Existing methods are typically evaluated with different backbones, preprocessing pipelines, and computational budgets, making it difficult to determine which components actually drive performance, how much they cost, and whether agentic inference is preferable to native video reasoning in the first place. We conduct a controlled evaluation of a diverse set of recent agentic video-reasoning systems across two strong contemporary backbones, with explicit token and monetary-cost accounting. Across Gemini 3 Flash and Gemma 4, most existing agentic frameworks fail to consistently improve over native video inference and often increase computational cost. We investigate two primary questions: (1) How much agentic framework complexity is necessary for effective video reasoning? (2) When, if at all, is agentic video reasoning preferable to just using the backbone directly? To answer the first question, we introduce a deliberately minimal Active Exploration Baseline and show that it remains competitive with substantially more elaborate agents. We then propose targeted extensions to this baseline, yielding SAVE (Simple Agentic Video Explorer). SAVE outperforms all evaluated prior agentic methods in five of six backbone-benchmark settings. Turning to the second question, our results indicate that the advantage of agentic exploration grows when dense processing would otherwise represent answer-relevant events too sparsely, particularly for long videos and temporally concentrated evidence. Overall, our results suggest that agentic video reasoning should favor simple frameworks over increasingly elaborate pipelines and focus primarily on long-form video, where selective evidence acquisition offers the clearest advantage over native inference.

title: Science Prediction Universe
abstract: Humanity has long sought to explain natural phenomena. Reliable prediction of experimental outcomes is a central test of our understanding of the processes that produce them. If artificial general intelligence (AGI) is to surpass human scientific capabilities, it must also predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans. Such capabilities could accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines, help address humanity's most pressing challenges, and improve human well-being. We introduce Science Prediction Universe (SPU), a benchmark of hidden experimental outcomes with 100 public verified tasks from chemistry, materials science, biology and medicine, and 16 private tasks from unpublished wet-lab experiments. Given an experimental setup and candidate conditions, an agent works with any resources it needs to rank the candidates by a measured outcome. We evaluate thirteen agent configurations spanning twelve frontier models across two harnesses (Codex and Claude Code). Current agents remain far from saturating wet-lab outcome prediction, with substantial performance disparities across models: on the public benchmark, configurations separate into two distinct tiers, with task-adjusted Spearman correlations ranging from 0.227 for the lowest-performing configuration to 0.478 for the best. Analysis of 1,155 scored public trajectories (227,103 tool calls) suggests that the bottleneck lies in scientific judgment rather than tool execution: agents rely on shared monotone priors, agreeing far more with one another than with experimental reality (0.52 vs. 0.33), and frequently compute trivial physical or chemical proxies that do not influence the final outcome.

title: The Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a Candidate Framework for Artificial Affective Regulation
abstract: Whether machines can feel remains unresolved. This article proposes the Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a candidate framework for studying one narrower target: regulation in an artificial agent whose internal variables are sensed and linked to a valence-like reward. The proposed index combines four provisional dimensions with a causal necessity gate; it is not a validated instrument. The manuscript reports a ten-seed tabular foraging pilot, but the original code and per-seed data were unavailable for this revision, so those values cannot be independently reproduced. A separate independent reimplementation tested two safe starts, 20 training seeds, and checkpoints at 1,200 and 2,000 episodes. Mean survival was often high, but paired checkpoint intervals included zero and seed-level failures remained. These findings establish limited feasibility under the reimplementation’s stated assumptions, not validation of MEQ or reproduction of the original pilot. A descriptive analysis of two unloaded robot-telemetry routines found different motion-current contrasts, but the records expose no controller channel or intervention and do not constitute an MEQ evaluation on a real system. The contribution is therefore a research proposal, a transparent account of preliminary evidence and measurement problems, and a staged plan for validation. None of the results bears directly on subjective experience.

title: Protecting Sensitive Knowledge Under LLM Unlearning: The Proxy Threat and a Superposition-Aware Defense
abstract: Machine unlearning lets the owner of large language models (LLMs) remove specific entities from a trained model without retraining from scratch. Existing machine unlearning methods focus on removing the requested entities while maintaining utility. However, we observe that the representations of distinct entities in an LLM may overlap in shared parameter subspaces, a phenomenon known as knowledge superposition. Removing one entity may then affect other entities. This exposes a new security threat: legitimate unlearning requests can be exploited to remove sensitive entities that were never requested. This threat is unlike data poisoning or backdoor attacks. We define the attack as the Proxy Unlearning Attack (PUA), which selects removable proxy entities superposed with a sensitive target. The attack can even occur unintentionally, when benign users accidentally remove entities superposed with a sensitive one. In response, we propose Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection (SAUP), a general defense framework that can be applied to unlearning requests to ensure a correct removal. SAUP performs in two stages. Before unlearning, it uses superposition detection to estimate which sensitive entities the request puts at risk. After unlearning, it decouples the shared representations and restores the affected entities, while keeping the requested entities suppressed. Our findings reveal that legitimate unlearning requests can be maliciously exploited through knowledge superposition. When dealing with unlearning requests, LLM providers need representation-level detection and recovery mechanisms to mitigate this threat and protect sensitive knowledge.

title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models on 12 of 15 and three foundation models, one general-purpose and two for biosignals, on 14 to 17 of 19, with none exceeding it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and it retained its performance when channels were missing.

title: agentrecount: recount every claim in an AI agent's report against your own data (formula, denominator, period, four verdicts)
abstract: agentrecount is a dependency-free Python tool for auditing the reports that AI agents write. Each claim of the report is entered with its formula, denominator and period; the tool recomputes it from the user's own tables (CSV or JSON) under the stated definition and under every alternative way of counting listed, and sorts it into one of four verdicts: holds as stated; holds only under one way of counting; partly false or misleading; not reproduced or not testable. It also lists the claims that arrived without a denominator or a period. The verdict scale and the procedure come from the case report AI Call Center Supervisor in a Live Company (payrollburn, part 1 of the series AI managers in a live company, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23926850), in which only one of nine checkable claims of the agent's own weekly report held exactly as written. The example data are synthetic. Python 3.10+, standard library only, no network calls. Part of the free Digital employees catalog at arsentev.ai/employees.

title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
abstract: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. Empirically, our method consistently outperforms standard parallel TTS approaches across benchmarks, while significantly improving token efficiency and reducing overall computation.

title: An Improved EfficientNet-B0 Model for Facial Emotion Recognition
abstract: Abstract Facial emotion recognition (FER) is increasingly built into interactive software, but reported accuracies are hard to compare because datasets, emotion sets and evaluation splits differ between studies, and few studies examine whether a larger backbone is worth its extra computational cost on the same data. This study develops and evaluates an EfficientNet-B0 model for five-class FER (happiness, sadness, anger, surprise and neutral) and compares it with EfficientNet-B1 and EfficientNet-B2 trained on the same images. FER2013 and the Real-world Affective Faces Database (RAF-DB) were combined, 1,470 duplicate or label-conflicting images and 19 unreadable files were removed, and a balanced set of 25,000 grayscale images (5,000 per class) was divided into 20,000 training, 2,500 validation and 2,500 test images, with no image shared between subsets. The model was fine-tuned in two stages from ImageNet weights using label smoothing, geometric and photometric augmentation, Mixup and CutMix. On the independent test set, EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 78.68%, a macro F1-score of 78.83% and a macro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.948, with class F1-scores ranging from 70.13% (neutral) to 87.78% (surprise). EfficientNet-B1 reached 79.76% accuracy, a difference that McNemar's test did not find significant (p = 0.107), while EfficientNet-B2, trained under a reduced schedule, reached 75.44% and was significantly less accurate (p < 0.001). EfficientNet-B0 used 36.6% fewer parameters than B1 (4.38 million against 6.90 million), needed 8.5 ms per image for single-image inference against 12.4 ms, required 40% less fine-tuning time and recorded the highest macro AUC of the three backbones. The trained model was deployed in a FastAPI web application that returns the predicted emotion with a confidence score. Within the conditions tested, EfficientNet-B0 gave the best balance between recognition performance and computational cost, while sadness and neutral remained the expressions most often confused with each other.

title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
abstract: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize termination lag--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. Our analysis reveals that 38--82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit. However, agents continue to expend substantial effort after correct patches, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35--37% for Qwen3-Coder and 54--60% for Laguna-XS.2 in successful runs on SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual. Agents spend most of these additional steps verifying their work and exploring the repository. In a small fraction of cases (1--8%), this continued activity leads agents to undo their earlier correct patch, leaving the final solution incorrect.

title: A Metalinguistic Axiomatic Theory of Intelligent Systems: Formal Structures of Cognition, Knowledge, and Theoretical Systems
abstract: English abstractThis work develops a metalinguistic axiomatic framework for cognition, knowledge, theories, intelligent systems, and AI. At the cognitive level, the framework distinguishes objectified items, registered meta-level interfaces, and residual metalanguage, retaining failure and unevaluability. Evaluation, object admission, name binding, and state writeback each have separate conditions. At the knowledge level, knowledge-base membership is distinct from verified or assertable status. Provenance, composite status, four-valued judgment, argumentation, tracing, and safe introduction serve distinct roles. At the theory level, theory objects comprise object and relation sets under co-rootedness and well-founded dependency conditions. Theory evaluation, transformation, and positioning have separate conditional interfaces. At the intelligent-system level, maintenance constrains optimization. Boundary, stable, and higher-order intelligence depend on stated criteria; AI generation and model scale alone do not establish these qualifications. Behavioral interfaces conditionally connect complete action, interaction goals and evaluations, and traceable joint descriptions. A six-step metatheoretical workflow organizes the deconstruction, reconnection, and reconstruction of existing theories. Task-relative textual and geometric representations organize theoretical expression and retrieval without replacing the underlying theory texts. The contribution combines theory-internal axiomatic or quasi-axiomatic reconstruction with cross-level interface organization. It makes domains, dependencies, admissibility, failures, and theoretical effects explicit. Empirical scales, engineering realizations, and system effectiveness require independent implementation and testing.中文摘要认知、知识、理论、智能系统与人工智能研究常使用相互分离的概念语言。产生结果与引入对象、保存信息与接受知识、改善输出与维持系统等不同任务,也因此容易混淆。本文建立一套元语言公理化框架,通过对象层与元层接口连接这些研究层次。框架区分已对象化项目、已登记元语言接口,以及当前对象语言不能吸收的元语言余项,并保留失败与不可评价。 在认知与知识方面,框架分别规定求值、对象引入、名称绑定与状态写回的资格。知识库成员不等于已验证或可断言知识。来源、复合知识标签、主显示、四值判断、论证、回溯和安全引入各有职责;它们不构成所有候选必经的流水线。 在理论层,理论由对象集及其中的关系对象集构成,对象集须满足共根与依赖良基条件。原始对象与基本原理由内部前驱读取,理论品质、变换和结构位置则通过各自的条件接口处理。 在系统层,维持约束优化,边界、稳定和高阶智能按明示判据区分。AI的生成与规模本身不证明这些资格成立。行为附录通过条件接口接入完整行为结构、互动目标与评估,以及可追溯的联合描述。行为分类不等同于趋人化或主体资格。 前四章的部分接口被组织为六步流程,并由四组异质方法示例说明。收束命题仅在各步资格与输入输出条件成立时连接环节;示例本身不独立证明这些条件。第8章规定任务相关的文本与几何表示,并区分假设与待定承接位。索引调用受答案覆盖、局部正确性和完整成本约束。 本文结合选定概念的理论内重建与跨层接口组织,明确各项内容的对象域或元层角色、资格、依赖、失败值与理论效力。工程实现、经验量尺和系统效果仍需独立实现与检验。 Full texts and supplementary materialThis record provides the full text in English and Chinese, together with separate English and bilingual Chinese-English theory-framework diagrams to support reading and cross-referencing of the main text. title: RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence
abstract: Aerial spatial intelligence (ASI) requires models to understand objects and spatial relationships across changing viewpoints and scales. Evaluating these abilities as models evolve calls for fresh physical observations, yet producing new aerial spatial questions requires repeatedly establishing entity identities, geometric references, and cross-view correspondences. We introduce RSLiveBench-UAV, a continually evolving vision-language benchmark driven by recurring acquisition of real UAV imagery. Its update protocol admits images captured after the preceding release and delays answer disclosure. An entity-centered production workflow uses geometry-assisted association to link repeated observations of physical vehicles, reuse human-verified attributes, and combine them with view-specific annotations and spatial references for traceable question generation. All tasks use deterministic scoring without model judges. We evaluate 30 general-purpose, remote-sensing, and embodied models on 35,491 question records from ten scenes, covering 17 tasks across 2D perception, 3D perception, cross-view perception, and reasoning. All 18 tested embodied models outperform the three selected remote-sensing comparators in Overall, although the strongest embodied model scores 43.29 versus 59.88 for GPT-6-Astra. Fine-grained vehicle recognition remains challenging, and performance varies across heights and camera pitches. Retrospective scene-group comparisons and rolling-window replay characterize score-pattern consistency under scene renewal. RSLiveBench-UAV connects fresh physical observations, entity-centered answer production, and systematic model evaluation to support continual assessment of ASI. Benchmark will release at https://rslivebench.space

title: Fooling Deep Neural Networks: A Strategyfor Mitigating DLSCA
abstract: Side-channel analysis (SCA), particularly deep learning-based SCA (DLSCA), threatens cryptographic implementations by automatically exploiting complex and nonlinear leakage and weakening countermeasures such as masking. Existing countermeasures against DLSCA mainly suppress, decorrelate, or obscure exploitable leakage. This work introduces Spoofing-based Mitigation (SPM), a leakage-shaping approach designed to mislead key-recovery attacks by biasing their key hypotheses. SPM introduces a controllable offset into AES intermediate-value computations and compensates for it to preserve the correct ciphertext, while shaping the relationship between measured leakage and the intermediate-value labels used for profiling. We implement SPM at the first-round S-box output and evaluate it at first-round and last-round attack points on an XMEGA128D4 microcontroller using a ChipWhisperer platform. Under the evaluated identity-label settings, the induced key’s rank rapidly reaches zero across seven CNN-based DLSCA models, two MLP-based models, and a template attack, while the correct key remains unrecovered. These results provide experimental evidence that leakage shaping can misdirect the evaluated key-recovery attacks. The collected dataset is publicly available to support reproducible research.

title: Auriga: Harness-Governed LLM Agents for Effective Throughput Optimization in Execute-Order-Validate Permissioned Blockchains
abstract: Effective throughput, the product of raw throughput and transaction success rate, determines the useful capacity of Execute-Order-Validate blockchains such as Hyperledger Fabric. Most prior work either tunes configurations to raise raw throughput, requiring many costly redeployments, or controls conflicts to raise the success rate, repairing them only after execution with kernel modifications. The few joint approaches tune only a small set of parameters and still rely on kernel changes to resolve conflicts. To address these challenges, we present Auriga, a non-invasive framework that jointly optimizes both factors through sample-efficient LLM-guided configuration search and pre-execution conflict prevention. A harness-governed multi-agent architecture coordinates LLM agents for parameter exploration, saturation-aware evaluation, and experience consolidation, with the harness controlling tool and memory access and retaining termination authority. For transaction scheduling, an LLM extracts symbolic AST templates from smart contracts offline. At runtime, the scheduler predicts read-write sets without executing them and partitions transactions into conflict-free groups. Across three benchmarks and conflict rates up to 70%, Auriga improves effective throughput by up to 6.0 times over default Fabric and 2.0 times over the strongest baseline. The tuning agent also discovers undocumented parameter dependencies, and ablation studies show the independent contributions of both subsystems.

title: A Semantic Representation Model for Geographic Features with Integrated Neighborhood Context
abstract: Geospatial data contains abundant temporal, spatial, and attribute information related to geographic entities, serving as a critical foundation for the development of new quality productive forces. Achieving effective semantic representation of geographic features is a key prerequisite for enabling intelligent data analysis and application. Spatial relationships are an essential semantic characteristic of geographic features and are among the most commonly introduced characteristics for representation learning in recent studies. However, current research primarily focuses on point-based features (such as POIs) or on converting line and polygon features into point features, leading to inaccuracies in representing spatial proximity between features, which in turn affects the representation outcomes. In this paper, a feature unit delineation method based on geometric shapes is proposed to better construct the proximity relationship graph between features. It enriches the semantic features of feature units using a large language model and trains an edge optimization model to refine the graph structure. Building upon iGCL, a semantic representation learning model for geographic features is constructed. Finally, using Xiamen Island and Nanchang City as study areas, experimental datasets are built by integrating OSM and Amap (Gaode) POI data. The performance of the proposed model is validated and compared with other models through three tasks: semantic overlap calculation, node classification, and node clustering. The results show that the feature representations obtained by the proposed model achieve the best performance across all tasks, fully demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority in geographic feature representation learning, thereby providing a foundation for subsequent intelligent geographic feature tasks.

title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. To study this vulnerability, we propose T-SemAttack, a transferable semantic attack based on a semantic encoder ensemble. By jointly drifting the representation spaces of multiple semantic encoders, T-SemAttack effectively disrupts the semantic content of speech while preserving perceptual quality, thereby inducing error features. We further analyze layer-wise representation drift and cross-model gradient alignment. Our findings show that perturbations can induce substantial shifts in deep semantic representations and that the input gradients of different surrogate encoders exhibit directional alignment. These observations suggest that shared adversarially sensitive directions in the input space may be a key factor underlying cross-model attack transferability. Building on these, we introduce ROSETok, a robust speech tokenizer that combines noisy training with robust semantic distillation to improve reconstruction fidelity and downstream SpeechLLM robustness. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets, 9 open-source and black-box ASR systems, and 4 LALMs demonstrate that T-SemAttack achieves strong transferable attack performance, while the proposed Robust Speech Tokenizer exhibits robustness under high-fidelity reconstruction and downstream tasks. Our code and demo are available at https://wxzyd123.github.io/t-semattack.

title: Algorithmic Opacity, Proxy Discrimination and Financial Citizenship in AI-Driven Credit Markets
abstract: Abstract: This article investigates the intersection of artificial intelligence, consumer credit, and financial governance, arguing that algorithmic opacity in AI-driven credit scoring does not eliminate discrimination but transforms it into an epistemic and governance crisis. Drawing on doctrinal legal analysis, comparative regulatory examination of Brazil, the European Union, and the United States, and an analytical reconstruction of the Apple Card case, the study demonstrates that historical biases are statistically reconstructed through proxy variables while the inherent opacity of machine learning models conceals these processes under a veneer of data-driven objectivity. The result is a structural deficit in evidence, contestability, and supervisory capacity that undermines the core pillars of financial citizenship: protection, participation, and trust. The original contribution lies in reconceptualizing algorithmic credit discrimination as a problem produced by opacity rather than solely by intentional disparate treatment, revealing that the absence of evidence of bias cannot be equated with evidence of fairness when the system under scrutiny is designed in ways that resist independent verification.

title: MLIRBench - A Benchmark and Dataset for Compiler and Hardware-Aware Reasoning
abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly popular in software engineering and have performed well on different programming tasks. However, it is still difficult to know whether these models truly understand program behavior or whether they mainly rely on patterns learned from their training data. This distinction is particularly important for intermediate representations (IRs), where operations, dataflow, and execution semantics are explicitly represented. In this paper, we introduce MLIRBench, a benchmark for evaluating how LLMs reason about MLIR programs. MLIRBench uses a multi-agent pipeline to generate program mutations, validate their behavior through execution, and construct reasoning tasks from torch and linalg program pairs. The dataset contains 1,768 validated pairs, including 888 linalg pairs and 880 torch pairs, labeled as EQUIV, DIVERGE, or ERROR. We evaluated nine models, including five open-weight and four proprietary models. Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved the highest hard-label accuracy of 92.65% across all 1,768 pairs, counting unsuccessful predictions as incorrect. Across its 1,768 scored predictions, it achieved an aggregate score of 74.18 and a judge-assigned result-behavior score of 5.04/10. These results show that strong semantic classification does not necessarily imply accurate prediction of detailed execution behavior, highlighting a gap in current LLM reasoning over compiler IRs. By exposing this gap through execution-validated program pairs, MLIRBench provides a reproducible foundation for studying semantic reasoning over compiler IRs and related tasks such as program repair and semantic classification.

title: Research on fine-tuning and application of domain-specific large language model for traditional Chinese medicine consultation
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient professional knowledge and low accuracy in question answering within the field of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) using general-purpose language models, this paper proposes a method for constructing a TCM question-answering model by fine-tuning a pre-trained language model. First, relevant TCM literature and diagnostic knowledge are collected and organized to construct a domain-specific question-answering dataset, achieving a structured expression of TCM knowledge. Second, instructions are fine-tuned on the pre-trained language model to adapt it to question-answering tasks within the TCM domain. Finally, experimental validation is conducted in TCM consultation and knowledge-based question-answering scenarios, and the model is compared with the non-fine-tuned model. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy and professionalism of the model's question-answering in the TCM field, demonstrating its potential value for intelligent TCM consultation applications.

title: Bipartite Concept-to-Token Language Modeling: Paraphrase-Invariant Mini Concept Planners with Context-Steered Token Expansion
abstract: Autoregressive token-level Large Language Models (LLMs) conflate high-level semantic planning with low-level syntactic realization, expending O(L2) self-attention compute across surface tokens even when underlying clauses represent deterministic, paraphrase-invariant concepts. Conversely, pure sentence-level Large Concept Models (LCMs) compress en- tire clauses into continuous embeddings but lose exact syntactic and lexical steering at branching transitions. We propose the Bipartite Concept-to-Token Architecture (BCTA), which decouples language modeling into two specialized networks: (1) a Stage-1 Mini Concept Planner that operates on canonical, paraphrase-invariant concept codes (map- ping synonymous spans such as “sun rises in the east” and “sun rises in eastern direction” to a single quantized representation SRIE) interleaved with structural steering operators (<$>) to predict the next semantic state (SSIW) in O((L/k)2) complexity; and (2) a Stage- 2 Context-Steered Token Expansion Model that frames the planned sequence [SRIE, <$>, SSIW]into fluent subword tokens conditioned on global entity premises (e.g., <we have one sun> → “The sun rises in the east and that same sun sets in the west”) and a lightweight residual detail bypass that preserves exact numerical and lexical literals. We formulate the complete composite objective combining Paraphrase-Invariant Vector Quan- tization, Anti-Collapse InfoNCE, and Context-Contrastive Margin losses, differentiate BCTA from concurrent multiscale concept architectures, and detail the exact implementation blueprint for both a 15.2M-parameter Mini Prototype and a 3.8B-parameter Expanded Model.

title: MediPFN: Amortized In-Context Nuisance Learning and Inference for Causal Mediation Analysis
abstract: Causal mediation analysis decomposes a treatment effect into indirect pathways through mediators and direct pathways through other processes. Tabular foundation models perform classification and regression through in-context learning, providing estimates of conditional means and propensity scores used in causal mediation analysis. Constructing confidence intervals from these estimates requires accounting for uncertainty introduced by fitting and combining several nuisance functions. We introduce MediPFN, an amortized inference framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to nuisance prediction and combines its predictions through a cross-fitted influence-function estimator. A separate head learns quantiles of the estimator's standardized error from simulated tables with known indirect effects. Supervised fine-tuning, symmetrization, and independent calibration then produce a confidence interval. We establish coverage bounds for the resulting intervals under standard assumptions. Across experiments, MediPFN attains coverage closer to the nominal level than several comparators. It also reduces the computational cost of uncertainty quantification, running 59.1 times faster than bootstrap in matched comparisons.

title: GTAGym: AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

title: Brandora: Automating Brand-Compliant Marketing Content Creation with Retrieval- Grounded Cloud Generative AI
abstract: General-purpose generative models used for advertising often invent prices, discounts, certifications and environmental claims that a brand cannot support. This paper presents Brandora, a hybrid edge and cloud generative AI system that drafts advertisement copy and visuals grounded in a company's own product catalogue and brand guidelines. A retrieval-augmented generation pipeline retrieves the catalogue records closest to a marketer's brief and always adds every mandatory guideline to the context of a locally hosted large language model, which returns a structured brief listing its sources and the requested details it could not support. A text-free prompt is sent to a serverless text-to-image model on Cloudflare Workers AI, and the approved copy is typeset onto the returned image, which avoids the malformed lettering that diffusion models produce. A reviewer approves every poster and each decision is written to an audit log. The paper also specifies extensions to the same architecture and an evaluation protocol of sixty briefs, including adversarial requests, for measuring guideline violations, grounding precision, image text artifacts, latency and reviewer effort. On 200 development queries, the hybrid retrieval stage ranks the correct product first in 97.5 percent of cases.

title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge.

title: Use First, Verify Later: AI Mathematical Discovery and the Operative Standards of Acceptance
abstract: When AI mathematical discovery outpaces human verification, social demand can force time-bound decisions about adoption. The HYC theorem distinguishes two directions: HYC1 identifies operative standards when duty-bound institutions cannot verify or abstain; HYC2 reconstructs such standards from decisions already issued without verification. Historical cases show that use, formal checking, and understanding can occur at different times. AI may also build on unverified results before human checks finish. Where society has no urgent demand, researchers can defer adoption, provided they retain time and an independently auditable record. Information saturation may undermine that capacity.

title: Il diritto di dubitare Privacy, pensiero critico e approccio Human-Tech nell'era dell'intelligenza artificiale
abstract: Nel confronto con l’intelligenza artificiale generativa, l’abilità decisiva potrebbe non essere formulare richieste semprepiù sofisticate, quanto preservare la libertà di mettere in discussione risposte convincenti. Il contributo propone unapproccio Human-Tech centrato su agency, verifica, protezione dei dati e responsabilità della decisione. Integrandopsicologia del ragionamento, studi sull’affidamento eccessivo all’AI e indicazioni istituzionali su privacy e alfabetizzazionedigitale, viene delineato un modello operativo in cinque movimenti: definire, proteggere, esplorare, falsificare eassumersi la decisione. Si esaminano esempi per scuola, formazione e contesti organizzativi, con attenzione alle nuovegenerazioni e alle implicazioni sociali della delega tecnologica. L’obiettivo non è contrapporre umano e artificiale, bensìprogettare relazioni con la tecnologia capaci di aumentare possibilità senza indebolire il giudizio.

L’obiettivo non è contrapporre umano e artificiale, bensìprogettare relazioni con la tecnologia capaci di aumentare possibilità senza indebolire il giudizio.

title: Adaptive Confidence-Aware Transformer–Graph Fusion Network for Robust Credit Fraud Detection
abstract: Currently, finding fraudulent transactions made with credit card systems is a major concern for the research community. The growth of online payment systems has increased transaction volumes. Attackers use increasingly sophisticated techniques, including identity theft, card cloning, and the compromise of online transactions, making fraud detection challenging for financial institutions. Traditional detection models rely on fixed rules and thresholds, which limit their ability to adapt to emerging fraud patterns; these systems are not flexible to deal with new and dynamic types of fraud. The literature shows growing interest in the development of datadriven intelligent systems for the analysis of transactional behaviors and the automatic recognition of suspicious activities. In this context, an adaptive confidence-aware transformer–graph fusion network model is proposed for reliable fraud detection in imbalanced financial transaction datasets. This study empirically investigates the two publicly available financial transaction datasets: ULB credit card and PaySim synthetic dataset which is a commonly used standard in the literature, examining fraud detection; these datasets have realistic distributional characteristics and anonymized variables. The graph-based fusion model is evaluated on PaySim, where it obtains 99% in accuracy, 96 % in F1-score, and 99 % in receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC). It improves recall and F1-score compared to individual transformer and Graph Sample and Aggregate (GraphSAGE) models and conventional machine-learning methods.

title: FViT: A Foundation-Tokenized Vision Transformer with Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Scale Ensembling for Deep Learning-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue morphology but is too costly for routine clinical use, motivating prediction of expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) images. FViT (Foundation-tokenized Vision Transformer) tokenizes a spot and its k nearest neighbours with the frozen foundation model Phikon, fuses the tokens with a small trainable Transformer with a relative-position embedding, predicts expression directly and by k-nearest-neighbour retrieval of measured training expression, and combines three neighbourhood sizes (k = 8, 16, 24) in a weighted ensemble. We evaluated FViT on two public cohorts, Her2ST (HER2-positive breast cancer, eight patients) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC, four patients), with leave-one-patient-out validation in which the gene panel, the retrieval parameters and the ensemble weights are selected without the evaluated patient. The ensemble reached a Pearson correlation of 0.180 (Her2ST) and 0.213 (cSCC) on the 50 most highly expressed genes (HEGs), but only 0.067 and 0.059 over all 1000 panel genes. Controls showed that neighbourhood fusion with relative position raised the HEG of direct prediction by +0.038 (Her2ST) and +0.045 (cSCC) over a centre-only model, that retrieval changed it by +0.002 to +0.004 on Her2ST and +0.007 to +0.010 on cSCC, and that the multi-scale ensemble differed from an ensemble of three seeds of a single neighbourhood size by −0.003 to +0.008. Under the same folds and panels, the released mclSTExp model (one seed, released settings) reached 0.141 and 0.177. In a section-level protocol, 99% of the retrieved weight came from other sections of the query’s own patient, and the ensemble’s retrieval gain fell from +0.013 to −0.002 when these sections were masked. Published results use section-level protocols and other gene panels, so they are not directly comparable. With eight and four patients, the findings are exploratory.

title: La inteligencia artificial y la protección constitucional de la propiedad intelectual en el Ecuador
authors: Patricia de las Mercedes Muñoz Alvarado
abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed intellectual creation processes, creating new challenges for legal systems in the field of intellectual property. In Ecuador, the Constitution of the Republic and the Organic Code of the Social Economy of Knowledge, Creativity and Innovation (COESCCI) recognize and protect copyright and other intellectual property rights; however, they do not specifically regulate works generated through artificial intelligence systems. This article aims to analyze whether the Ecuadorian constitutional framework is sufficient to ensure the protection of intellectual property against the challenges arising from the use of AI. To achieve this objective, qualitative documentary research was conducted through the analysis of national legislation, specialized legal doctrine, and comparative law. The study examines the evolution and operation of artificial intelligence, the criteria of authorship and ownership of AI-generated works, the protection mechanisms established in Ecuadorian law, and the regulatory approaches adopted by different jurisdictions. The findings reveal that the Ecuadorian legal system maintains a traditional concept of authorship limited to natural persons, resulting in regulatory gaps concerning works created or assisted by artificial intelligence. It is concluded that an update of the national legal framework is necessary to balance the protection of intellectual property rights with technological innovation while ensuring legal certainty and compliance with constitutional principles.

title: DECO-Net: An Improved Transformer Model with Dual-Evidence Attention and Counterfactual Ordinal Learning for Sentiment Analysis of Student Educational Reviews
abstract: Sentiment models now read the open comments in student evaluations of teaching (SET), and their outputs can inform decisions about teachers. Current models treat negative, neutral and positive as unordered classes and compress each comment into one vector. Mixed comments that praise one aspect of teaching and criticise another are therefore pushed to a pole, and a negative comment can be reported as positive. These models are also rarely tested outside their training platform. This study proposes DECO-Net, a dual-evidence counterfactual ordinal network. Two attention poolers measure praise and complaint evidence separately. Their difference gives a sentiment score, and a cumulative-link ordinal head places a neutral band between the two poles. A polarity-directional counterfactual objective requires each evidence channel to fall when its own tokens are deleted. DECO-Net was trained on 18,116 RateMyProfessors comments with professor-disjoint splits. It was evaluated with pre-specified hypotheses on fresh seeds, two encoders and two unseen sources, Coursera and University of Waterloo reviews. In-domain macro-F1 did not change significantly. Without any target data, DECO-Net with DeBERTa-v3-large raised macro-F1 by 2.1 to 2.4 points on all three external test sets, in five of five seeds (Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.047). Negative–positive reversals fell by 12% to 50%, and neutral recall rose from 0.531 to 0.605.

title: APLICAÇÕES ÉTICAS DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA EDUCAÇÃO: DESAFIOS E PERSPECTIVAS
abstract: A integração da Inteligência Artificial (IA) no cenário educacional contemporâneo tem suscitado debates profundos sobre seus impactos e, sobretudo, os dilemas éticos inerentes à sua adoção. O presente estudo parte da necessidade crítica de alinhar o uso dessas tecnologias com diretrizes que protejam a privacidade dos estudantes e evitem a propagação de vieses algorítmicos. O problema que motiva esta pesquisa reside na implementação de ferramentas de IA opacas, conhecidas como "caixas-pretas", sem a devida reflexão sobre suas consequências sociais. Diante disso, o objetivo geral deste artigo é discutir os dilemas éticos da IA na educação e apresentar o desenvolvimento do protótipo de software "O Questionador" como uma prova de conceito (Proof of Concept) voltada à transparência algorítmica. Como objetivos específicos, busca-se analisar os riscos associados ao uso de dados escolares e descrever a arquitetura de um sistema que justifique pedagogicamente suas decisões. Para alcançar tais propósitos, adotou-se uma metodologia de pesquisa aplicada, complementada por uma revisão narrativa da literatura. Como resultado, o desenvolvimento do protótipo demonstrou a viabilidade técnica de implementar a transparência algorítmica na prática, permitindo que o sistema exponha a regra lógica de recomendação de estudos diretamente ao aluno. Conclui-se que implementar a transparência e a explicabilidade em softwares educacionais, mesmo utilizando lógicas determinísticas como base, é tecnicamente viável, exibindo ao aluno a regra que gerou a recomendação.

title: SwarmPNM: A Single-Trajectory Adaptive Optimizer with Positive–Negative Momentum and PSO-Inspired Attraction
abstract: SwarmPNM combines an adaptive second-moment estimate and positive–negative gradient momentum with attraction towards the lowest-loss weights stored along a single training trajectory. The attraction is inspired by particle swarm optimization, but the method does not maintain a particle population. We specify the update, analyze the attraction locally under Hessian assumptions and obtain a conditional regret bound for an auxiliary strongly convex projected-gradient model with controlled perturbations. Experiments cover 15 analytic test functions, molecular classification with MolCLR-pretrained GIN and GCN encoders on the blood–brain barrier penetration (BBBP), beta-secretase-1 inhibitor (BACE) and human immunodeficiency virus replication-inhibition (HIV) datasets, and nuclear cross-section regression with a multilayer perceptron. SwarmPNM attains the highest mean ROC–AUC in five of six molecular dataset–encoder combinations. In the four-library nuclear comparison, it has the lowest mean absolute error and the highest coefficient of determination; a separate three-seed nuclear experiment under a different protocol favors AdamW. Repeated-run, sensitivity and ablation studies establish that the contribution of attraction depends on the task and tuning, with the learning rate having the largest observed influence in the analytic sensitivity tests. We also report the additional computational cost relative to AdamW. The auxiliary theory does not establish convergence of the complete nonconvex optimizer.

title: Classical Simulation of Quantum Channel Families: Unbounded Cost Separation and Sharp Noise–Error Scaling
abstract: When the input measurement is fixed across a channel family, the simulation of binary output tests allows test-dependent responses, whereas preparing a quantum output requires one normalized state per recorded branch. We prove an unbounded separation between the optimized outcome costs of these tasks for families admitting a common mother measurement. The channel choices are specified by classical descriptions. For an explicit family of qubit channels, six outcomes suffice for all binary tests, whereas the exact channel cost is finite at every positive level of additional depolarizing noise and diverges as the noise vanishes. The family is the image of an explicit CPTP processor with a fixed finite-dimensional program and qubit input and output. For noise fraction λ and uniform output-channel diamond-norm error ε, the minimum common-measurement cost has the sharp order (λ + ε)^{−2/3} for 0 < λ + ε ≤ 1/2, both when channels are approximated independently and when the approximating family is generated by a single CPTP processor on the same spaces. The lower bound holds for arbitrary approximating channels subject only to the common-measurement budget. At each sufficiently small positive noise level, one finite common mother serves an entire full-dimensional process neighborhood of radius proportional to λ, throughout which the same cost law and six-outcome binary-test simulator persist.
